reader.decision: Go with the queued export: enqueue render_invoice_csv on the `documents` queue, return 202, and email a signed link. Before merging, confirm the storage.put signature and that taskq has no tight task time limit.
reader.decision_reason: The message shows the 504 comes from the 30s idle timeout while the whole CSV is built in memory. Queuing removes that cause and also frees the saturated web workers (12/12). Streaming would leave workers held for minutes per export, and tenants needing more than 300s would still be cut. The contract change is the cost, and the message gives no sign that any client needs the file in the response body.

reconstruction.problem: export_invoices in app/exports.py builds the full CSV (1,840,211 rows) in a StringIO before sending any byte. The build takes about 240s total (18s query plus 222s writing). gw-billing has idle_timeout_seconds=30, so it closes the connection and returns 504 for the largest tenants.
reconstruction.what_breaks: Large tenants never receive a file. Retries start more long builds. At month end about 900 exports saturate the web workers (12/12) and push /invoices p99 to 9.4s, up from 0.4s on 2026-10-15.
reconstruction.fix: Enqueue render_invoice_csv(tenant_id, recipient) on the taskq `documents` queue, modelled on render_invoice_pdf. The handler returns 202. The task writes rows to a file, calls storage.put and storage.signed_url, then mailer.send with the link. Also change app/exports.py, add jobs/invoice_csv.py, and add one line to docs/exports.md.
reconstruction.cost: The contract changes: callers get a 202 and an email instead of a file. Any client that parses the CSV from the response body will break. `documents` shares capacity with invoice PDFs at the month-end peak. The storage.put signature and taskq time limits are unverified.

follow_up_questions: Does any known client parse the CSV from the response body of GET /exports/invoices.csv?
Does storage.put accept a file or file path, and does taskq enforce a task time limit that a roughly 4 minute export could hit?
reader.closing_answer: Make export_invoices a queued job with an emailed signed link. Streaming from the handler is the fallback only if a client must get the file in the response body.
